title: Harness rust-analyzer runs check-on-save flycheck as a local workspace cargo check against lane checkouts, bypassing the lane shim
wanted_capability: When a dispatched harness child opens a rust-analyzer session for a checkout whose builds are lane-routed (a ~/lanes/<name> checkout), flycheck must not spawn a local `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` on the control-plane host. Either the LSP session initializes rust-analyzer with check-on-save disabled (initializationOptions `checkOnSave: false`, or `check.overrideCommand` pointing at the lane shim), or the harness routes rust-analyzer's cargo invocations through the same cwd-keyed shim that bare cargo uses. Observed: a glm dispatch in a pool lane spawned rust-analyzer, whose flycheck ran `~/.rustup/toolchains/stable-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin/cargo check --workspace --message-format=json --manifest-path ~/lanes/bpool6/blackbox/Cargo.toml --keep-going --all-targets` on the Mac after every file save, with two rustc processes at 96% CPU compiling the root crate over NFS into ~/Library/Caches/blackbox/ra-target. That is the exact local cold-build path the lane contract exists to prevent, and it competes with every sibling lane on the host.
missing_primitive: Rust initializationOptions in crates/bro-lsp/src/lib.rs build_init_params (only Java gets options; rust-analyzer keeps its checkOnSave=true default), or a lane-aware flycheck command for host-built rust-analyzer sessions
fallback_used: None during the session; the local checks were left running. Operator-side mitigation would be BLACKBOX_RUST_ANALYZER_BIN pointing at a wrapper that passes --config for checkOnSave=false, or dispatching Rust edit work with the lsp surface disabled.
evidence: crates/bro-lsp/src/lib.rs build_init_params: initialization_options is Some only for Language::Java, so rust-analyzer runs with checkOnSave enabled

crates/bro-lsp/src/lib.rs spawn_session / apply_lane_environment / lane_host_build_env: lane-rooted sessions strip the lane shim from PATH and set a host CARGO_TARGET_DIR, so flycheck's cargo check runs on the host
design/refactor-tools/rust/rust-isolate-surface.md lane host-build section: budgets one cold host build of proc macros and build scripts, not a full workspace check per save
PROJECT.md Where Heavy Work Runs: cargo/rustc route into the lane pod only when invoked by bare name from a lane cwd
notes: Triage: the harness LSP client is crates/bro-lsp (bro-harness depends on bro-lsp), not crates/bbox-lsp; the original evidence pointed at the daemon crate. The host-side spawn for lane checkouts is deliberate (proc-macro dylib format mismatch), so the fix is scoped to flycheck, not to where rust-analyzer runs.
